summary.intent: Run Session 5 of the v1-alpha launch plan: implement WP E (NativeName registry-equivalent package identity) and WP I (relative workspace: directory index), then address lead follow-ups on PR #561: a review finding about historical tag ownership and a sibling PyPI check.
summary.outcome: WP E (#561) and WP I (#563) were pushed with signed commits and green gates. Cargo, then PyPI, historical default-tag ownership was reverted to a single literal-name comparison via regression tests. The final fix commit was being created and not yet pushed, with mutation re-run and shas report pending.

repo: Package identity: NativeName (callisto-model identity.rs) is keyed on PEP 503 for PyPI and lowercase plus -/_ for Cargo, exact elsewhere. Used for E100 duplicate detection, selectors and [[package]] rules, but not for historical tag ownership.

Default tags carry the literal declared spelling (`name@version`), so history ownership (may_have_held_name_at, TagIndex, aggregate baseline) must compare literal names in every ecosystem, otherwise a foreign ecosystem's tag gets credited after rename/removal.

The plan's claims were partly wrong: ReleasePackageId.name need not key on NativeName (it would reorder stored rosters), release_decision.rs needs no edit, and no Cargo equivalence code existed before E.

Repo gates are just pre-push, just lint, just doc-check and just test. AGENTS.md also requires just ci before marking ready, which was not run. Commits must be signed with GitHub verification reason valid; local sig can show E.
Changesets are added via `callisto add --package cargo/callisto-cli:patch --summary ...`.
Mutation testing uses cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff; the diff filter must cover crates while excluding tests, or only a few mutants are found. An empty Hash::hash is an equivalent mutant.
Glob patterns (PackagePattern::matches_native, pattern.rs:72) still match manifest spelling, not equivalence.

code.finding: may_have_held_name_at returned early on equivalent-name match, letting a foreign-ecosystem tag be attributed to a renamed package. Fixed by literal comparison.
TagIndex accepts a tag when history ownership says the name was held, so it inherits the history equivalence bug.
Aggregation takes the foreign tag's version as baseline, which is where the mis-attribution surfaces.
native_owner map keyed on NativeName is the duplicate-detection fix.
Duplicate relative workspace: resolution removed in favor of the graph's single NpmDirIndex, with a lazy once-built index.

friction: The first mutation run on E covered only 3 mutants because of a bad path filter, and re-runs took about 15 minutes each.
Fixes interacted: review-driven changes left a duplicate `use super::*;` and unused-parameter lint failures that needed extra gate loops.
A script edit hit the wrong worktree and removed the wrong `use super::*;`.
BSD sed and the compound-command guard slowed down scripted edits.
#561's audit fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0542, fixed only by #560, so no ignore was added.
The original Cargo equivalence in history was an over-reach that the review caught late.
open_items: Commit for the PyPI literal-name fix is made but not yet pushed, and gates, mutation run (--in-diff on d69bd794e plus the new commit) and sha report are pending.
Need zero missed mutants or one-line equivalent-mutant notes in the PR body, including the empty Hash::hash one.
Add to the PR body why or how the PyPI sibling reproduced.
Rebase #561 then #563 after #560 merges, resolving the benches/commands.rs conflict if it recurs.
Owner must decide whether E's changeset should be marked **Breaking:**, since workspaces with equivalent names now fail with E100.
Glob patterns like pypi/my-* still match manifest spelling.
Owner should confirm that Cargo foo-bar/foo_bar is E100 as a settled decision.
Run just ci before marking PRs ready.
Delete the wp-e and wp-i worktrees after merge.
